children: Evercore ISI's latest iPhone survey indicates Apple
should enjoy a stronger-than-normal upgrade cycle and benefit from higher average selling prices.

"We see not just room for units to do well, but critically, we think pricing could be >20% driven by a combination of ASP increases, higher-priced SKUs, and a shift up in memory configurations," said Evercore analyst Amit Daryanani in a Friday investor report.
"Pricing trends continued to grow, with our survey reflecting an aggregate ASP of $1,374, up nearly 28% and well above our long-term survey average," he said.

The survey found that 53% of the nearly 4,000 consumers taking part plan to buy an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max. This is up from the average of 51%. It also discovered that 32% of respondents intend to buy the Pro Max compared to 29% in last year's survey. Fourteen percent said they will purchase Apple's new product, the iPhone Duo, compared to 9% last year who said they would buy the new iPhone Air.

"Our 2026 iPhone survey points to a solid upgrade environment, with 61% of respondents planning to purchase an iPhone. This is slightly higher than last year's survey of 59% and marks the second strongest response in our survey's history and well above our survey average of 45%," Daryanani said.
Beyond the iPhone, there was a slight increase in respondents planning to upgrade their Apple Watch and AirPods.
Evercore retained its Outperform rating on Apple and increased its price target to $380 from $365.

title: Over half of Apple users plan to upgrade to iPhone 18: survey
